Comparison

HeyGen vs Synthesia

A side-by-side look at HeyGen and Synthesia, using the details in each tool profile.

Quick take

Choose HeyGen when your priority is: translating existing video into other languages while keeping the original speaker's voice. Choose Synthesia when your priority is: multilingual corporate training and communication video at scale.

HeyGen vs Synthesia at a glance

CriteriaHeyGenSynthesia
CategoryAI Video GeneratorsAI Video Generators

Key features
  • Video Translate preserving the speaker's own cloned voice across 175+ languages with lip sync
  • 700+ stock avatars
  • Instant Avatar from a 2-minute webcam recording
  • Avatar IV for photo-to-video animation
  • Interactive Avatar for real-time conversational video
  • Photo Avatar
  • 240+ stock avatars plus custom personal avatars (studio-recorded or webcam)
  • 140+ languages and voices with accurate lip sync
  • one-click translation of an existing video into other languages
  • AI Video Assistant turning documents, URLs or PowerPoint into video
  • branded templates and brand kit
  • screen recording
Advantages
  • Video Translate with voice cloning and lip sync is the standout capability here - keeping the original speaker's voice across languages is far more persuasive than a stock avatar
  • Instant Avatar from a 2-minute webcam recording lowers the barrier dramatically
  • API-first design makes personalised video at scale practical
  • faster and cheaper than Synthesia for many use cases.
  • Language coverage at 140+ is unmatched and includes proper Arabic support, which matters enormously for MENA organisations
  • updating a video by editing text rather than reshooting is transformative for training libraries
  • strong enterprise compliance posture (SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001)
  • SCORM export slots into existing LMS estates.
Limitations
  • Voice cloning raises serious consent and deepfake concerns - HeyGen has controls but the misuse risk is real and organisations need a policy
  • enterprise compliance documentation is thinner than Synthesia
  • translation quality varies notably by language pair
  • credit and minute metering across two separate pools is confusing
  • Avatars remain identifiably synthetic and some audiences react poorly - it is presenter video, not cinematic video
  • minute allowances are restrictive on lower tiers and enterprise pricing is steep
  • no camera movement or visual storytelling beyond a talking head with slides
  • strict content policy blocks some legitimate uses

Pricing notes

HeyGen

Free with roughly 3 videos per month, up to 3 minutes each, watermarked. Creator around $29/mo ($24 annually) with unlimited video length on some plans and no watermark. Team around $89-99/seat/mo ($69 annually) with more credits, brand kit and collaboration. Enterprise custom, annual, with API volume, SSO and dedicated avatars. Video Translate and Interactive Avatar are metered separately by minute on most tiers.

Synthesia

Free plan with roughly 3 minutes of video per month, limited avatars and watermark-free basic output. Starter around $29/mo ($18-24 annually) with roughly 10 minutes/month and 1 seat. Creator around $89/mo ($64-67 annually) with roughly 30 minutes/month, custom avatar options and more features. Enterprise custom, annual, with unlimited or high-volume minutes, custom avatars, SSO, SCORM and dedicated support - typically five figures per year.

Prices change often. Confirm on the official pricing pages: HeyGen ↗ · Synthesia ↗

Frequently asked questions

What is the main difference between HeyGen and Synthesia?

HeyGen: AI avatar video platform strongest at video translation with voice cloning and lip sync - it takes an existing video of a real person and reproduces it in another language in their own voice with matched mouth movement. Synthesia: Enterprise AI video platform built around realistic presenter avatars.

When should I choose HeyGen over Synthesia?

HeyGen is listed as best for: translating existing video into other languages while keeping the original speaker's voice. Synthesia is listed as best for: multilingual corporate training and communication video at scale.

Do HeyGen and Synthesia have a free plan?

HeyGen: Yes. Synthesia: Yes. Check each official pricing page, as plans change.
